thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Streaming proxy p99 latency breach detected in us-west-2 (service: streaming-gateway). Pager routed to #incidents and @oncall-miguel. See metrics: https://ops.metrics/internal/streams/alerts/3777770000

oncall-miguel: acked. I’m booting into the runbook now. ETA 2m.

sre-amy: I’m looking at the proxy group for us-west-2, seeing a sudden climb in socket write latency + TCP retransmits. p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.8s on the tail.

eng-runtime-lee: any change in model variants or batch configs pushed in the last hour? CI shows a canary deploy 55 minutes ago but nothing obvious.

support-jia: A handful of customers reported streaming stalls and partial responses — CS ticket 89432 notes clients saw long pauses then resumed. No wide-scale disconnects yet.

oncall-miguel: ok, immediate triage: 1) Isolate whether source is client backpressure or proxy buffering. 2) Check proxy keepalive/timeouts and upstream connection pools. 3) If needed, enable fallback short-window flush to reduce tail.

eng-runtime-lee: running quick dashboards. I see abrupt increase in client window occupancy for connections passing through proxy -> signs of slow consumers. But also proxy egress queue depth rising. Could be a combined slow-consumer + kernel buffer exhaustion.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-15T09:10:12Z to streaming-gateway completed on 35% hosts 54 minutes ago. Patch id: cg-2026-03-15-kt.

sre-amy: can we check proxy logs for 'write blocked' or 'EAGAIN' during the window?

eng-runtime-lee: tailing logs now:
```
2026-03-15T09:24:12Z gateway[proxy-pod-12]: write() returned EAGAIN, queued 12 chunks for conn xxxxx
2026-03-15T09:24:13Z gateway[proxy-pod-12]: client-slow-consumer: conn xxxxx rx-window 16384 -> 2048
2026-03-15T09:24:14Z gateway[proxy-pod-12]: upstream-kv-cache-hit, flush deferred
```

support-jia: customers on websockets reported occasional blank frames, then stream picks up. Matches the EAGAIN symptom.

oncall-miguel: hypothesis: sudden wave of slow consumer clients causing proxy write backpressure -> proxy buffer grows -> upstream serving runtime delays chunking/kv cache flush -> per-request tail latency spikes.

eng-runtime-lee: I can flip a mitigation: reduce the proxy's per-connection write-buffer target and enable aggressive flush policy to favor smaller chunks out. This will increase tokens per second slightly but should reduce p99. Anyone object?

product-ethan: as long as we include a note for customers re: increased rate of small frames. Prefer to avoid disconnecting users.

sre-amy: do it. Also increase keepalive probes to detect dead sockets faster (reduce idle timeout from 120s -> 30s) for this region as a short-term mitigation.

eng-runtime-lee: rolling config change now to proxy group:
```
kubectl set env deployment/streaming-gateway PROXY_WBUF_TARGET=64KB PROXY_AGGRESSIVE_FLUSH=true PROXY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=30
```

incident-bot: Change request submitted. Patch id cg-3777770000-flush. Rolling to 100% of canary in 2m window.

eng-runtime-lee: applying to 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%. Monitoring metrics.

sre-amy: within 90s I see p95 drop from 420ms -> 180ms, p99 dropping from 1.8s -> 560ms. Socket retransmits also declining. Good signal.

support-jia: CS reports early customer feeling better; one customer still saw a brief stall (ticket updated).

oncall-miguel: next steps: 1) keep the aggressive-flush config for next 2hrs, 2) instrument detailed tracing to capture per-connection window backpressure, 3) plan longer-term fix: graceful drop of extremely slow clients or explicit flow control headers.

eng-runtime-lee: adding tracing flags now:
```
kubectl annotate deployment/streaming-gateway tracing=slow-consumer-detail
```
Also starting a job to correlate client IPs with retransmit counts.

sre-amy: also alerting infra to check for any kernel-level socket queue exhaustion (net.core.wmem_max / rmem_max) on the hosts — we might need sysctl bump if this pattern recurs.

product-ethan: Can we check whether certain SDK versions cause more slow-consumer behavior? CS noted two clients on older JS-SDK 0.9.2.

support-jia: yes, both tickets reference JS-SDK 0.9.x. I can reach out to ask for logs and recommend upgrade.

eng-runtime-lee: observed that under aggressive flush, token throughput rose ~6% but cost impact within acceptable bounds for mitigation window. No regression in correctness.

incident-bot: NOTE: No full-customer outage. Impact: brief p99 SLO breach for ~12m window, degraded streaming experience for a subset of websocket clients (approx 0.4% of connections).

oncall-miguel: marking incident as mitigated for immediate customer impact. Will keep watch for 1 hour and hand to oncall-runbook for follow-up. Assigning postmortem to @eng-runtime-lee and @sre-amy.

eng-runtime-lee: logging follow-up actions in TICKET-377777: 1) implement client-slow-drop policy for extremely low read windows 2) server-side flow-control headers 3) upgrade telemetry for connection-level metrics 4) evaluate bumping host socket buffers for region.

sre-amy: I’ll open infra PR for kernel params and schedule a canary.

support-jia: I’ll queue customer comms draft for CS review — short note explaining brief latency spike and mitigation steps + SDK recommendation.

product-ethan: include link to KB: optimizing client consumption for streaming (once updated).

oncall-miguel: Great. Closing live triage. If p99 creeps up again, page escalation to eng-runtime owner. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident thread closed as mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:26:05Z. Postmortem pending.
